issue_context.title: Add manual "Check for updates" button in settings
issue_context.body:
**Describe the new feature:** 
-------------------------------------
Some times the internet connection are unstable or too slow that take too long time to update, least I am.
The game are not trying to update everytime when start if you close it before downloading update finish

Please add a _**Check Update**_ button in settings below _**Open Osu! Folder**_ for manually start update or check update everytime the game starts

**Proposal designs of the feature:**
-------------------------------------

Add a _**Check update**_ button in settings below **_Open Osu! Folder_**
Check for update everytime the game starts
comments: From what I can see the game *should* be checking for new updates every launch - but a manual check button might be an interesting proposal, I suppose.
Will eventually be added back, but super low priority. May be a good first issue for someone looking for something to do.

review_comments: No, don't silently return when you shouldn't be called, throw `NotSupportedException` here.
`CheckForUpdateAsync` shouldn't be called if the `UpdateManager` itself isn't capable of doing it, that should be identified as a bug.

I don't follow. It's a public method. Are you expecting every usage to first check the bool? That sounds like really bad API. Why don't we just make UpdateManager null and throw a nullref then? Isn't the point of making it abstract to simplify external implementation?
Right, you have a point there. It's fine in this way then.

> I don't follow. It's a public method. Are you expecting every usage to first check the bool? That sounds like really bad API. Why don't we just make UpdateManager null and throw a nullref then? Isn't the point of making it abstract to simplify external implementation?

I thought about making UpdateManager abstract too, but it seems to go beyond of just checking for updates.

At this point I would suggest splitting UpdateManager into 2 classes for their own functionality, that being a class for checking for new updates, and another one for doing the startup work when a new update has been applied.

This way we can stick to abstracting the checking process and make it null on not deployed builds/mobile versions.
I can't see the gain of splitting the two things. Sounds like extra complexity for not much gain.
are you sure this doesn't regress anything?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22963120/81357283-87427480-90d3-11ea-819e-b0d980ca27b5.png)
osu!'s update check at startup still works, so this is a yes from me.
